record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Given 0 < delta <= 1, does there exist n0(delta) such that for every n >= n0(delta) and every family F of subsets of [n]^2 with |F| at least delta times 2^(n^2), there are A and B in F with A contained in B and B\A equal to X^2 for some subset X of [n]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ and let $[n]^2 = [n]\times[n]$. For a subset $X\subseteq[n]$, write $X^2 := X\times X \subseteq [n]^2$.

Given $0<\delta\le 1$, does there exist an integer $n_0(\delta)$ such that for every $n\ge n_0(\delta)$ and every family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $[n]^2$ satisfying
$$|\mathcal F|\;\ge\;\delta\cdot 2^{n^2},$$
there exist members $A,B\in\mathcal F$ with $A\subseteq B$ and 
$$B\setminus A \;=\; X^2 \quad\text{for some } X\subseteq[n]\,?$$
